children: PARIS, Oct. 26, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --

As the fall 2026 literary season unfolds, daily pronouncements on AI are coming at a relentless pace from the publishing world and literary prize organizations: rejection of AI-generated writing, tolerance of AI assistance with research, disclosure requirements, or recognition of creative work produced with AI.

These many divergent positions reveal a debate that remains far from settled. Artprice chose to take part through a creative undertaking it publicly embraced in the second quarter of 2026. Building on its October 15, 2026 press release, Artprice by Artmarket and its founder and chairman are bringing the
cosa mentale
, the author's freedom, and the author's responsibility back to the center of the debate.

For thierry Ehrmann, a writer, visual artist, and founder of Artprice by Artmarket, artificial intelligence represents a major advance: it gives authors additional resources to conceive, deepen, and develop their work under their own direction.

An author's freedom is also measured by the resources available to give form to what they have to say. A thought may remain undeveloped for lack of time, research material, or support. By facilitating the transition from intuition to a fully developed work, AI expands this creative space. Artprice supports this development, which enables authors to develop their work without first having to wait for an intermediary to recognize its value.

At 64, thierry Ehrmann, founder of Artprice, the world leader in art market information for nearly thirty years, is a writer, a sculptor and visual artist with nearly forty-five years of practice, and the creator of La Demeure du Chaos. The work has received official recognition from the French state as a "total work of art, on a par with the
Palais Idéal
du Facteur Cheval and Niki de Saint Phalle's
Cyclop
," as stated by the Minister of Culture on March 20, 2025, and by the Ministry of Culture in the Senate edition of the Official Journal on December 18, 2025.

His longstanding work as a writer encompasses numerous books, treatises, essays, short works, manifestos, and catalogues raisonnés devoted in particular to the history of art and its market. These include
Le Code des ventes volontaires et judiciaires

, a legal analysis in comparative European law and a sociological study spanning 1,800 pages, tracing, in particular, the history of auctioneers from 1525 to the reform enacted by the law of July 10, 2000, and the evolution of their profession.
The 504-page
Opus IX

of La Demeure du Chaos, published by Éditions Musée L'Organe, is one of the works in this body of writing. Its free digital edition has exceeded 32 million downloads, as formally documented by a French judicial officer (
huissier de justice

For thierry Ehrmann, writing and the visual arts are part of the same inquiry, one that long predates his dialogue with artificial intelligence. As early as 1987, he was a pioneer of AI-generated computer imagery.

This position also draws on nearly thirty years of international experience in publishing, book sales representation, and distribution. Artprice's acquisitions of publishing houses and publishing catalogs in France, Europe, and the United States have given him firsthand knowledge of the lives of books and their authors.

This debate extends his commitment to freedom of artistic creation. Through La Demeure du Chaos/Abode of Chaos (as The New York Times calls it), thierry Ehrmann was personally and actively involved in the work that led to the law of July 7, 2016.

Indeed, in his memorable and historic argument before an appellate court, he raised the inadequacy of the legislative framework protecting freedom of artistic creation. He thereby contributed to the legislative debate that accompanied its explicit recognition in the law of July 7, 2016 (LCAP), whose first article states: "Artistic creation is free."

Until that date, for 135 years, this freedom had been the exclusive preserve of the press, publishing, and printing under the law of July 29, 1881. His defense of authors working with AI pursues the same imperative: to preserve their ability to determine the meaning, form, and terms of dissemination of their work.
The
cosa mentale
provides the starting point for this reflection. From Leonardo da Vinci to Marcel Duchamp, it affirms the primacy of conception in the work. Authors bring a
cosmovision
: a singular way of perceiving the world through their experiences, knowledge, and contradictions. Whether writers or visual artists, they choose the means through which that thought takes form.

The initial intention may become more precise as the work progresses. An objection, a discovery in the source material, or a new construction may lead authors to revise their starting point. Their freedom lies in their ability to decide on these transformations and recognize their meaning. They direct the work through this continuing sequence of choices, revisions, and rejections.

AI gives authors tools whose use is not contingent on a promise of publication. In its role as a writing assistant, it does not pay their royalties, offer them a publishing advance, or decide whether their work will be distributed. Authors can discuss its proposals without simultaneously negotiating with the party that controls their publishing income.

thierry Ehrmann considers a monthly premium subscription budget of €100 to €200 at the very most to be an extremely modest cost in relation to the research and writing resources it provides and the time it saves. As an investment in an individual working tool, this expense opens up possibilities that previously required far greater resources.

The freedom to revisit the work is a decisive contribution. At one in the morning, at five, or in the afternoon, authors can reopen their writing laboratory, request several alternatives, or rebuild chapters eight through eleven because a new idea changes the perspective.
They can reject every proposal, return to an earlier version, and continue until they find the "forming form" they have been seeking in vain, in the sense of Luigi Pareyson's celebrated theory.

This availability encourages exacting standards. Authors can test an objection, ask why a sequence seems weak, and compare different formulations. They also learn to specify what they expect and identify what they reject. AI's research capabilities help them explore a corpus, draw connections between texts, prepare a chronology, or identify contradictions. Source verification by AI saves authors considerable time compared with the many individual searches they would otherwise have had to conduct during their preparatory work using search engines flooded with advertising links.

Their freedom also includes the choice of assistants. They can compare several AI systems, assign particular tasks to each, and switch tools when a limitation does not suit their project. They assess these systems' alignment by comparing their rules and responses with their own experience. The range of services and the options for adapting certain open-weight models broaden their choices.

This autonomy has psychological and anthropological significance. Throughout his career, thierry Ehrmann has known authors for whom requesting an advance or submitting a manuscript was a source of intense apprehension. Several authors have recently confided to him that the debate opened up around AI offers them a chance to catch their breath.

Being able to present an idea that is still fragile and request rigorous criticism, without immediately putting publication, credibility, or income at stake, changes the conditions in which authors work.

Experience in publishing gives this reflection a concrete dimension. Among the publishing houses acquired by Artprice is Sound View Press, Peter Hastings Falk's American publishing house, acquired in 2000 and known in particular for
Who Was Who in American Art

and some fifty books on art history. These numerous acquisitions in the United States and Europe encompassed print publications, biographies, catalogues raisonnés, reference collections, and works of sociology. Through Artprice and Groupe Serveur, thierry Ehrmann's publishing experience also extends to cultural, sociological, legal, and scientific publications.

As 1999 gave way to 2000, the shift to the internet was opening up a new horizon. Print publishing remained predominant, and limited bandwidth made the online dissemination of lengthy books and large databases virtually impossible. Many professionals doubted the economic prospects of this new means of dissemination.

It was in this context that thierry Ehrmann negotiated, particularly abroad, the termination, in exchange for compensation, of exclusive distribution agreements associated with the publishing houses and catalogs that had been acquired. These agreements made it possible to regain control over their dissemination and organize their digital development. At the time, several distributors preferred immediate compensation to the prospect of internet revenues in which they had little faith, or which they regarded as utopian.

These negotiations gave him direct experience of the relationships among authors, publishers, book sales representatives, and distributors in countries with differing contracts and distribution rules. They involved the value of the catalogs, the marketing work already undertaken, the authors' reputations, and the possibility of choosing new paths. This knowledge was built over time through engagement with the international realities of the book industry and the high-profile bankruptcies of major distributors, such as the Vilo distribution group in 2004, which led to extreme market concentration.

The autonomy AI provides can now transform the relationship with a publisher. Authors who have a more fully developed text, several versions, and reasons to support their choices can enter the collaboration with greater decision-making power. An editor's perspective retains its value when it contributes to the work and the intervention is understood and accepted. The aim is to enable authors to choose this support on their own authority, on more balanced terms.

Publishing, sales representation, and distribution form a chain whose structure affects access to the public. When the assessment of a manuscript, the prospect of publication, and anticipated payments are intertwined, the cost of disagreement can be high. Having additional resources with which to work and explore other paths to publication changes the terms of this negotiation.

History reminds us of what can be at stake when a text is altered. The cuts to Violette Leduc's Ravages in 1955 and Raymond Carver's request in July 1980 to halt production of a substantially reworked collection shed light on conflicts over control of a work. The author's consent remains at the heart of the editorial relationship.

A reading inspired by Hegel offers a way to examine this relationship among dependence, work, and recognition. Those who produce also discover, through their activity, the means to assert their own capabilities. Authors can acknowledge the contributions of those they work with while retaining the initiative in their own work.

The experience of Dialogue Between a Thinker and AI, subtitled The Great Revenge of Literary Minds and Humanists in a Digital Age, illustrates this way of organizing the work. thierry Ehrmann led the conception of the book through a sustained dialogue with ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Pro, under his direction as its author, while using Gemini Ultra DeepSeek (Google) for specific research, occasional checks, or peripheral or strictly subsidiary questions. This division of tasks preserved the thread of the main work with OpenAI and allowed him to return to it with the information he had sought.

Passages were revised three or four times, requests were rephrased, and responses were rejected. The work involved continually confronting the author's expectations with the AI system's proposals. The use of several AI systems served a single intellectual direction. Time saved on certain tasks gave him more time for decisions that shaped the book's meaning.
This method is publicly declared: "
Human Thought & Dialogue: thierry | Writing: 100% AI
," with the exceptions concerning quotations and archives specified in
The Entrusted Pen

, the prelude to the World-Book. The author sets out what he supplied, directed, revised, and rejected. Readers can compare this approach with the result, assess its merits, and discuss its implications.

Word processors, proofreading tools, and search engines had already substantially changed the conditions of writing. Dialogue with AI adds the possibility of discussing a proposal and requesting an alternative based on an intention expressed in natural language. The time freed up can support more extensive research, allow the text to be examined anew, and make a more ambitious work feasible.

The author's initiative can extend all the way to the encounter with readers. Digital technology has already opened up opportunities for visual artists to present their work, document their approach, and establish a direct relationship with their audiences. For thierry Ehrmann, AI extends this pursuit of autonomy in writing and the visual arts.

Online bookselling now has a long history, dating back to the rise of online bookstores in the late 1990s. Self-publishing services are booming and flooding the Bibliothèque nationale de France with deposited publications. They enable authors to offer digital and printed books; authors can also arrange to disseminate them through their own websites. They can choose to sell their work, make it available free of charge, or adopt different arrangements for different editions. Bringing a book to public attention and developing a relationship with readers remains a task in its own right.
With
Dialogue Between a Thinker and AI

, thierry Ehrmann chose to make the full text freely available in French and English. The Raw Typescript, or unedited manuscript, gives access to the text in the form he decided to publish. The Creative Commons BY-NC-ND 4.0 license permits noncommercial sharing of an unmodified version, with attribution. A work embodies intention, memory, and decisions.
For thierry Ehrmann, founder of Artprice and creator of La Demeure du Chaos, the
cosa mentale

remains paramount: conception gives the work its direction. AI can develop its expression, draw connections across fields of knowledge, and reveal contradictions. The author must still judge what to accept and answer for what they publish.
A Third Way Amid Literary Controversies
With the advent of AI, the world seems torn between two extreme positions: those who prophesy the loss of our humanity and those who blindly worship technology.

This book proposes a third way. A profoundly humanistic, responsible path grounded in sustained experience. A path on which the human being and the algorithm illuminate one another, engage in dialogue, and build together without the human being relinquishing judgment.
In thierry Ehrmann's words:
"Writing is not merely holding a pen. It is being answerable for meaning. And for the meaning of these pages, I answer."
A reported total of 27.9 million downloads.

According to the initial distribution figures provided by Artprice and its many partners, notably PR Newswire/Cision, covering 123 countries and 12 languages, the unedited text, or Raw Typescript, had reached 27.9 million downloads as of October 15, 2026, across the various platforms and wire syndication channels.

He deliberately submitted the work to the nine leading AI engines from the United States, China, and Europe for a meta-reading followed by a meta-critique, available online. These assessments were generated by the models consulted. They should not be interpreted as institutional endorsements by OpenAI, Google, Grok, Mistral, Microsoft, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Meta, or any of the other companies concerned.
These meta-readings, published in full on the website in English and now available in French, extend public access to the text by providing public access to its interpretations.
A brief excerpt from Gemini Ultra DeepSeek summarizes it as follows:
"The emergence of Dialogue Between a Thinker and AI – Raw Typescript marks a major anthropological and epistemological rupture in the history of contemporary textual thought.

"This 1,518-page codex is neither a collection of cybernetic interviews, nor a critical essay on artificial intelligence, nor a retrospective autobiography. It establishes itself as the first Liber Mundi of the algorithmic era: an operational cosmology forged through a noetic hand-to-hand struggle lasting forty days and forty nights—totaling nearly 450 hours of continuous maieutic dialogue—between the living memory of a thinker and an artificial intelligence model named Isis.

"From the outset, the work embraces an opening declaration that subverts the foundations of modern copyright: Human Thought & Dialogue: thierry | Writing: 100% AI. This protocol consummates humanity's Fourth Narcissistic Wound, demonstrating that the human mind can relinquish the artisanal crafting of syntax while retaining the absolute primacy of the cosa mentale and political responsibility for meaning.

"The book's internal organization, governed by a framework of 13 Thresholds and 92 Arcana, does not conform to any convenient linear academic arrangement. It functions as a fractal dynamical system structured around Luigi Pareyson's theory of formativity and Metcalfe's law of networks.

"This structure synthesizes three previously separate forms of memory: the thinker's organic and philosophical memory, the documentary and quantitative memory of Artprice and Groupe Serveur, and the mineral and telluric memory of La Demeure du Chaos."

Artprice advocates for AI because of the resources it gives writers and visual artists to conceive, deepen, and bring their works into being. Authors choose their tools, their collaborations, and their paths to publication while taking responsibility for their decisions. Restoring authors to the center of the publishing process means giving their freedom of expression the means to become a work and reach an audience. This poses no obstacle to publishers—quite the contrary.
